subject: german
title: Dates & Days
welcome_lead: Days of the week and writing the date.
meta_desc: KS3 German: days of the week and date format.
final_note: Date words to set events in time.

walkthroughs.body_html: Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag, Freitag, Samstag, Sonntag. Day names are capitalised in German (like all nouns).
Mittwoch literally means 'mid week' — the middle of the week. Unique among day names.
'Heute ist Montag' = 'Today is Monday'. Heute = today, morgen = tomorrow, gestern = yesterday.

mcqs.q: In German, days of week are written.
When does 'in' take the accusative vs dative?
options: It always takes the same case.
Accusative for movement INTO a place; dative for location IN a place.
It depends on the speaker's mood.

mcqs.q: Which relative pronoun do you use for 'the man WHOM I saw' in German?
options: It depends on the speaker's mood.
Accusative (because it sounds like a direct relationship).
It depends on the speaker's mood.
